claim: The speakers position email as an existing business interface for delegation, records, and customer communication rather than as a replacement chat client.
The live application receives a typed verified webhook, routes by recipient, fetches content or attachments, calls an AI transformation, and sends a reply.
A normal forwarded message omitted full authentication headers, so the verification demo returned only 70 percent confidence.
note: Observed in the live demo. The confidence number is product output, not an independent security assessment.

claim: The image extraction route did not handle a message without an image and failed to send the expected explanatory response.
The proposed production design places the full inbound email on a queue and uses worker limits to control sender, customer, and global concurrency.
The proposed state model separates events from actions so user changes and multiple actors can be tracked against the same event.
The proposed queue is keyed by email thread to prevent concurrent processing of two messages in the same conversation.
Before writes and sends, the worker should check for a newer thread message, discard stale work when safe, and rerun from the latest state.
If an irreversible action escapes before a correction arrives, the next run must receive that outbound action as context so it can respond consistently.
